A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CausalPitfalls study. All 30 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments evaluating ten LLMs, a branding-bias experiment, human-grading validation, and a debugging comparison (Tables 3–9).

after.justification: v3 retains original ten-model benchmark results, branding-bias outcomes, human-grading validation, and debugging results (Tables 3–9).

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, direct and code-assisted prompting, GPT-4o rubric scoring, and the debugging variant remain identical (Section 2; Appendices C and H).

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same six causal-pitfall categories, fifteen challenges, and branding-bias and Dutch research-funding scenarios (Section 2; Appendices B and D). Newly cited studies do not introduce evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The same ten LLMs participate in Tables 4–5 and 7–9, and the same three models appear in the branding comparison in Table 3. The added citations are not new evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Difficulty levels, dataset sampling, scoring metrics, prompting procedures, the 150-response stratified human-validation sample, and the one-attempt debugging protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: The branding manipulation, funding-data analysis, difficulty and execution-error analyses, and debugging comparison are retained without revision (Sections 3–4; Appendices D and H).

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including the funding-data statistical checks and human-grading aggregation. No run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, GPT-o4-mini retains causal reliability scores of 40.72% for direct prompting, 43.03% for code assistance, and 45.15% with debugging (Tables 4 and 9); the overall human-grading gap remains 0.11 (Table 6).

T1.justification: The normalized-score and grading-gap definitions, causal assumptions, and appendix DAGs are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about benchmarking statistical causal pitfalls, evaluating reliability, and identifying limitations of current LLMs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic bias, random variation, uneven benefits from code assistance, and code-generation failures remain unchanged, as do the stated reliability limits and future directions.

D1.justification: Appendices C and F retain the same prompts, ten-row data preview, single NVIDIA A100, 1000-token maximum, and medium reasoning-effort setting. Code and data access statements and the repository target are unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1 and 1.2 add five cited works: Lin et al. (2025a, 2025b), Yu et al. (2025), Luo et al. (2025), and Du et al. (2024), with corresponding bibliography entries. Existing positioning and the benchmark-coverage comparison in Table 10 remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Textual edits are limited to inserted citation groups and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. The surrounding prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added citations change paragraph wrapping and redistribute bibliography entries across pages 10–12. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–10 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 expands background citation coverage through five references appended to existing statements, without adding substantive discussion or clarification. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and all appendices remain unchanged; the limited bibliographic and layout edits produce no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
